items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Demonstrated experience designing and building user experiences for complex, data-rich applications, with attention to usability, accessibility, and performance for technical and non-technical users.
Experience conducting biomedical research in academia or industry.

Experience participating in multi-stakeholder open source communities: distributed decision making, navigating uncertainty, building consensus, coordinating paid and volunteer contributors, mentoring new members.
Experience extending or contributing to JupyterLab or related open source projects.
Experience reviewing code through open discussion and iterations on GitHub. Demonstrated track record using issues and pull requests (or similar) for transparent and distributed project management.
Experience structuring and analyzing complex and multi-modal datasets, ideally following and contributing back to open standards.
Advanced experience with planning for real-world deployment and creation of feedback mechanisms across an interdisciplinary team.

Applies advanced software concepts to plan, design, develop, modify, debug, deploy, and evaluate highly complex interface, software, and/or infrastructure solutions in interdisciplinary research collaborations.

20% Contributes to and supports the maintenance and sustainability of 1-4 projects within the scientific open source ecosystem. Maintenance can include issue triage, code and documentation review, contributing new features, mentoring new contributors, continuous integration testing, and release management.
10% Develops project plans as part of an interdisciplinary team, delivers allocated tasks, and communicates progress regularly.

5% Analyzes existing highly complex open source software or works to formulate logic and devises algorithms for new modular and composable software systems. Understands and applies industry practices, open source community standards, and department policies and procedures in depth.

5% Enables collaborators to design, implement, reproduce, and extend highly complex data analyses to address real-world research problems, including accessing data from varied multi-modal processing pipelines, working directly with domain scientists and open source communities as appropriate.

5% Stays up to date on applicable research and software engineering standards, including applications of agentic AI for science (new models and tools, agentic architectures, and evaluation methods), and security and accessibility practices. Implements cutting-edge practices into software and protocol standards, meeting UC Berkeley-specific policy requirements and national and international standards as applicable.

5% Prepares and approves or obtains approval for user and developer documentation. Initiates and oversees changes in development, maintenance and system standards. Sets the technical requirements for software specifications, engaging across open source communities as appropriate. Communicates technical requirements to interdisciplinary experts and trainees with varied technical expertise.
5% Serves as technical lead for one or two software development projects of moderate to broad scope. Meets with interdisciplinary project teams and provides regular updates on progress.

5% Advances the work of the UC Berkeley Open Source Program Office (OSPO) by demonstrating the value and impact of open source practices. Delivers trainings and provides technical and community mentorship to members of the UC-wide OSPO network. Participates actively in monthly meetings and workshops.

A curious mindset and appetite for navigating complexity and uncertainty. A track record of scoping and delivering on requirements from interdisciplinary teams of domain experts and trainees with varied technical expertise.

Proven track record building tools that are used by academic research teams to conduct cutting-edge innovation in the life sciences, physical sciences (astronomy, physics, chemistry), and geosciences, and/or the social sciences, humanities, and public health.
Self-motivated and works independently and as part of a team. Able to learn effectively and meet deadlines.
Advanced programming skills, including Python and TypeScript expertise.
Excellent project leadership and management skills.

Demonstrated software development and maintenance skills: version control with git, testing, continuous integration and/or continuous deployment with GitHub Actions or similar. Advanced knowledge of secure software development.
Advanced skills associated with software specification, design, modification, implementation and deployment of large-scale scope.
Demonstrated ability to understand functional needs and how systems can support those needs, particularly in the context of leveraging existing functionality in scientific open source libraries.

Demonstrated effective communication and interpersonal skills. Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization and at academic and industry conferences.
Demonstrated complex problem-solving skills.
